title: Skip Zhangjiajie's 430m Glass Bridge — Look Below | China Travel Expert
description:
Everyone queues for Zhangjiajie's Grand Canyon Glass Bridge — 430 metres long and about 300 metres above the canyon floor. It's a thrill. But the real show is what's underneath it.

Those quartz-sandstone pillars rising out of the canyon are the landscape that inspired the floating Hallelujah Mountains in Avatar. The bridge is a 10-minute adrenaline hit; the pillars, forest and mist around it are what you'll actually remember. Walk the glass if you want the photo — but give yourself time on the rim trails and viewing platforms where the pillars stack to the horizon.

🧭 Expert Tip: go right at opening. The deck holds up to 800 people and fills fast — early light and thinner crowds make both the walk and the photos far better.

张家界大峡谷玻璃桥长 430 米、距谷底约 300 米；但真正的主角是桥下那片启发了《阿凡达》的石柱群。
